rationale: The finite-shape splitter, singleton bypass, per-batch limit rule, input-index restoration, and failure-policy choices provide a usable semantic baseline. They cannot be adapted in place because plan construction immediately invokes effects, hidden environment/registry state remains authoritative, and resource/authority/cancellation contracts are absent. Extract the pure plan semantics and rewrite execution as a typed ordered traversal; parallel eligibility must remain a separately proven interpreter decision.

rationale: The existing left-to-right aggregation is useful as a replay observation, but CollectResult and nested raw dictionaries are not a sufficient canonical failure/receipt contract. Mixed failures remain top-level completed, errors are heterogeneous, provider acknowledgements are optional scalars, queued is not distinguished from authoritative completion, and per-element receipts are not durable. A wrapper would preserve these ambiguities. Reimplement a typed ordered fold in the successor package and use the legacy fold only for bounded parity/replay comparisons.

source_evidence.claim: C3.2 is a frozen locator-only cell and originally grants no eligibility or migration authority.
Legacy results use loose dict/list payloads and optional provider_job_id/provider_type/provider_status/attempt_count fields without typed receipt or authority semantics.
The fold is input-order left-to-right, sums counts, appends errors, stable-deduplicates links/job IDs, and retains per-batch raw metadata, but initializes top-level status as completed.
Crawler dispatch maps provider status/job ID/attempt count into CollectResult; queued/scheduled/running are normalized to completed at the collect layer.
Source-library execution performs project-bound job logging and effects, then separately builds terminal/frontdoor/authority/compat projections.
Existing integration evidence checks provider_type, queued status, provider_job_id, attempt_count, and empty errors across collect and compatibility surfaces.

Existing fixtures preserve legacy fields, fallback errors, authority/compat projections, and provider handoff metadata, but do not establish durable receipt ownership or mixed aggregate status semantics.
Celery callers primarily return meta.raw or counter fallbacks, so typed status/error/receipt information can be collapsed at caller boundaries.

The architecture requires named observational compatibility with failure/authority/resource preservation, per-cell receipt fields, independent successor fold implementation, rollback, and no P2 selection during P1 audit.
The architecture-mandated legacy collect interpreter has not been implemented.
